subject: Inference pattern matrix for Dedicated proposal - Novacorp
messages:
From: Cara Long <cara.long@novacorp.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@novacorp.com
Date: Fri, 01 Sep 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial traffic extract and baseline — Dedicated sizing

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this. Attaching a condensed telemetry export we pulled from our prod edge for the last 30 days. The CSV contains: timestamp, route, prompt_type, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, user_session_id.

Topline: daytime transactional traffic (search + summarization) is steady; we see heavy bursts around product releases (roughly weekly) and a daily evening spike from 19:00-20:30 PST. Typical median response length is ~120 tokens; 95th percentile pushes to ~2.2k tokens for long-form generation.

We're evaluating a Dedicated pool to get predictable latency during launches — primary ask is an initial sizing recommendation and an outline of how Redwood would handle burst windows.

Attachments: novacorp_sample_telemetry.csv (CSV, 54KB), peak_window_summary.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

—Cara
Cara Long
Head of Platform Ops, Novacorp
cara.long@novacorp.com
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Cara Long <cara.long@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Sep 2028 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial traffic extract and baseline — Dedicated sizing

Hi Cara — thanks for the telemetry, very helpful. A few clarifying items before we run a sizing pass: 

1) Prompt mix: can you confirm the percent split across (a) short transactional (<= 64 tokens), (b) medium (65–512 tokens), (c) long-form (>512 tokens)? Your CSV gives token counts but if you have a pre-aggregated prompt_mix row that helps speed things up.
2) Concurrency semantics: are sessions pinned (session affinity) or stateless per request? If pinned, what's the typical session duration and average parallelism per user_session_id?
3) SLA targets: what p99 token-generation latency are you aiming for during peak? Any absolute latency ceilings for interactive flows?
4) Model variants: are you planning to use a single model family, or will requests fallback to smaller quantized variants under pressure?

We can do an initial ballpark offline and then propose a 60‑minute sizing workshop (workshop link below) to validate assumptions and review a GPU mix (A100xL / H100 / q8 variants) recommendation.

Proposed time for workshop: Thu 09/07 16:00-17:00 PT — does that work?

Thanks — looping Marissa and Karthik for the sizing pass.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Cara Long <cara.long@novacorp.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Sep 2028 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial traffic extract and baseline — Dedicated sizing

Markus/Cara — quick internal notes and a starter hypothesis before the workshop: 

- Looking at the CSV sample, token distribution skew is high: ~70% short, ~25% medium, ~5% long-form but the long-form drives peak GPU-time due to KV cache and larger KV memory.
- For predictable p99 during 95th percentile peaks, recommend targeting an A100xL-heavy pool for initial commit to support long-inference tails; mix plan: 60% A100xL, 30% H100, 10% q8-optimized instances for short/cheap paths.
- Autoscaling policy: keep steady baseline to cover sustained 75th percentile and enable rapid burst capacity with pre-warmed instances for the known evening windows (19:00–20:30 PST).
- Batching config: small continuous batching (max_wait_ms=20) for short flows, and adaptive batching disabled for long-form to avoid added latency.

Questions for Cara (to validate):
- Are there hard session-affinity requirements (cookie-backed routing) that would prevent pooling?
- Can you share a 24-hour sample (UTC timestamps) broken down by route so we can simulate queuing behavior?

I'll draft a sizing sketch ahead of the workshop and attach it.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Pre-Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Cara Long <cara.long@novacorp.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 08 Sep 2028 07:49:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial traffic extract and baseline — Dedicated sizing

Thanks — answered inline:
- Prompt mix: roughly 68% short, 27% medium, 5% long-form. I attached a small 24-hour route breakdown per your ask (UTC).
- Session affinity: mostly stateless for search; only the personalization endpoint pins sessions for ~10–15 minutes. Affinity affects ~8% of requests.
- SLA: we want p99 generation latency <= 750ms for short flows during peak; for long-form it's acceptable to have higher latency but p95 should stay under 4s.
- Model variants: yes, we plan to route to smaller quantized variants for cost-sensitive endpoints; long-form must hit the larger family.

Attachments: novacorp_24h_route_breakdown_utc.csv (CSV, 18KB)

See you all on Thu, workshop time works — will invite our infra and product leads.

—Cara
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Cara Long <cara.long@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 08 Sep 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial traffic extract and baseline — Dedicated sizing

Great — thanks for the 24h sample, Cara. Attached is a short prework agenda and our initial sizing sketch (high level) so your team can review before the workshop. Key asks for the workshop:

- Confirm the exact model families and any quantization constraints.
- Share a representative 1‑hour high-resolution trace (1s granularity) if possible — we use this to simulate queueing during bursts.
- Any compliance or private-deployment constraints we should include in the pricing sketch.

Workshop invite: Thu 07 Sep 2028 16:00 PT (calendar invite sent)
Prework doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cD3eNovacorpSizing

Looking forward to it — we'll come with a GPU-mix table and a draft commitment vs burst-cost sensitivity matrix.

—Markus
